transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Monday, August 3. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Locked, loaded ... and put on hold: Another bewildering Trump pivot on Iran. President Trump announced a halt to a threatened military strike against Iran for now. He cited requests from Iran and other nations for deal finalization. Diplomatic efforts are reportedly underway with mediators facilitating discussions between Washington and Tehran. Meanwhile, domestic political challenges and internal party criticism are growing for the President. 10,000 cases pending in SC for 10 yrs, 80,000 in HCs for 30 yrs. Despite significant investment, court infrastructure and technology have not reduced decades-old case pendency. Over ten thousand cases remain pending in the Supreme Court for more than ten years. High courts across India have over eighty thousand cases pending for over three decades. The law minister cited judicial responsibility and judicial vacancies as reasons for the delays. 39 medals, top-five finish: India ends CWG 2026 with several historic firsts. With several medal-rich sports missing from the programme because of financial constraints in hosting the Games , after the event was moved from Victoria in Australia to Glasgow , expectations were lower than in previous editions. Even so, India found success in new events, celebrated new athletes and produced several landmark performances. Jeff Bezos warns Mamdani on NYC taxes, slams wasteful spending. Jeff Bezos commented on New York City's proposed pied-à-terre tax. He suggested that aggressive tax increases could negatively impact tourism and competitiveness. Bezos also criticized targeting individuals, calling it a villain strategy. He argued that government spending inefficiencies are a greater concern than taxation. West Asia war uncertainty keeps businesses on edge. Businesses face significant cost management challenges due to ongoing West Asia conflict. Commodity inflation and freight charges create persistent planning uncertainties for companies. This instability may lead to postponed capital deployment and fewer new job additions. Consumers can expect widespread price increases across various products and services. Househelp apps cross 1L orders as prices fall to rupees 29. Snabbit and Urban Company's InstaHelp platforms each completed one lakh house-help jobs on Sunday. Intense competition pushed hourly household work prices down to twenty-nine rupees in some areas. Urban Company offered thirty-minute services for nineteen rupees, a significant discount. InstaHelp promises quick service for various household chores and has expanded rapidly. NTA floats tender to secure offices, exam material 24x7. NEW DELHI: After a paper leak exposed weak links in India's biggest entrance examination, National Testing Agency (NTA) is moving to put its premises, confidential records and examination material under round-the-clock watch. SC warns Punjab for ignoring 15-yr-old ruling on dues to Himachal Pradesh. The Supreme Court criticized Punjab for its resistance to implementing an old decree. Attorney General Venkataramani proposed a cashless settlement for power dues. Himachal and Haryana agreed to the proposal, while Punjab raised objections. The court warned Punjab of consequences if it fails to comply. Meet Roy Kim, 13, who turns air moisture into water for farms. In a remarkable feat of ingenuity, a young student has created technology that converts air moisture into potable water. This device stands as a sustainable beacon for farmers struggling with inadequate water supply. Featuring a Peltier module for condensation, it smartly monitors water delivery and environmental factors through advanced sensors. Roy Kim aspires for his invention to play a significant role in alleviating the global water challenges faced by agriculture. Monsoon Session: Congress set to stall House over Ram temple donation scam. NEW DELHI: Signaling continuing disruption in Parliament in the coming week, Congress has accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah of avoiding Parliament at a time when the Opposition has been raising the crucial issue of Ayodhya donation scam. Nanaji Deshmukh Awas Yojana: How workers can avail rupees 1.6 lakh housing aid. In Gujarat, registered construction workers have the opportunity to benefit from financial support aimed at housing through the Shree Nanaji Deshmukh Awas Yojana. To qualify, applicants must have been registered with the welfare board for a minimum of two years. Following the acquisition of an e-Nirman Card and house allotment, they can submit their applications. Those approved will receive rupees 1.6 lakh to assist in home ownership.

transcript.text: Moving to business, the economy and the markets. Gold Gains as Iran Talks Ease Concerns Over Interest-Rate Hike. Gold advanced after US President Donald Trump said fresh negotiations with Iran would begin later Monday, raising hopes for a breakthrough in the months-long conflict that would ease energy-driven inflation. Yen Bears Face Risks on Joint US-Japan Action, Strategists Say. Strategists say the coordinated intervention between Japan and the US increases the risk for anyone betting against the currency. President Donald Trump said the US joined a currency-market intervention that lifted the yen last week as a sign of friendship with Japan. Gold Dips as Traders Eye Dollar Recovery Against Yen, Fed Path. Gold fell as an intervention-driven rally in the yen stalled, helping the dollar snap a five-day run of losses. Yen Traders Brace for More Intervention With US at Japan's Side. Currency traders are on high alert for more joint intervention by Japan and the US when trading gets underway in Asia on Monday after coordinated operations in Tokyo and New York last week triggered a dramatic rebound in the yen. The one-way trade in semiconductor stocks that has defined equity markets this year is coming unglued, triggering stomach-churning volatility as investors grow increasingly concerned that the fire-hose of artificial intelligence spending won't continue. If oil prices remain contained and global tensions continue to soften, Indian equities could be positioned for a more sustained uptrend in the months ahead. Major OPEC nations have agreed in principle to another token increase in their production quotas for September, a move that would complete the theoretical revival of supplies halted in 2023 and give them scope to add more barrels once the Middle East war ends. During the week, the BSE Sensex gained 2,034.87 points (2.67 percent ), while the NSE Nifty advanced 616.15 points (2.59 percent ). Andy Burnham pushes for written UK constitution. Parle has launched a limited edition Tiramisu flavour of its iconic Melody toffee exclusively on Blinkit, with the pack explicitly carrying a 'celebrating India-Italy friendship' message. The Telangana High Court has ruled that taxpayers cannot lose Section 54F capital gains exemption solely because a builder delayed completing or registering a home. The judgment says delays beyond the taxpayer's control should not defeat the tax benefit if the investment has already been made. While banks get more flexibility in pricing bulk deposits, retail FD investors will see greater transparency and uniformity in interest rates.
